```{python}
#| include: false
import sys
from coolpath import ROOT, load_config
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "notebooks"))
from _site import table, md, fig, chart, pct, num, C
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
cfg = load_config()
s5, s6, s10 = table("phase_05_stats.json"), table("phase_06_stats.json"), table("phase_10_city.json")
days = " and ".join(pd.Timestamp(d).strftime("%B %-d") for d in cfg["study"]["dates"])
year = pd.Timestamp(cfg["study"]["dates"][0]).year
```

## Pipeline

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(f"""1. **Heights.** 2022 LiDAR: ground, buildings and trees at 1 m.
2. **Shadows.** Every hour from 8:00 to 19:00 on {days}, {year}, a ray from every 2 m of sidewalk towards the sun: *building
   shade* if a building, bridge or the ground blocks it, *tree shade* if only trees do, otherwise sun. The sun of an hour sits at
   half past the hour before (15:00 = 14:30), as in the heat model.
3. **Heat.** SOLWEIG turns the same heights and the weather into the **UTCI**, how hot it feels, at every square metre.
4. **Sidewalks.** Each sidewalk gets, per hour, its metres of sun, tree shade and building shade, and its UTCI.
5. **Routes.** Each walk has three routes: **shortest**, **shadiest** (shade cost) and **coolest** (heat cost).""")
```

## The cost of a sunny metre

The shadiest walk uses the cost function of Wen et al. (2025):

$$C = L_{\text{sun}} + (1 - 0.5\,\theta)\,L_{\text{tree}} + (1 - \theta)\,L_{\text{building}} + (1 - 1.5\,\theta)\,L_{\text{indoor}}$$

A sunny metre costs 1, tree shade 1 − 0.5θ, building shade 1 − θ, an indoor metre 1 − 1.5θ. θ grows with the distance already walked, so shade matters more the longer the walk:

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "θ as a function of distance already walked."
t = cfg["routing"]["theta_curve"]
x = np.linspace(0, 1500, 300)
th = t["a"] / (1 + np.exp(-t["k"] * (x - t["x0"]))) + t["b"]
f, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 3))
ax.plot(x, th, color=C["cool"], lw=2.5)
for d in (300, 800, 1200):
    y = t["a"] / (1 + np.exp(-t["k"] * (d - t["x0"]))) + t["b"]
    ax.scatter([d], [y], color=C["sun"], zorder=3)
    ax.annotate(f"{d} m: θ = {y:.2f}", (d, y), xytext=(6, -14), textcoords="offset points", color=C["dim"], fontsize=9)
ax.set(xlabel="distance already walked (m)", ylabel="θ", ylim=(0, 0.65))
chart(f)
```

With θ near 0.2 for the first 500 m, a short walk only leaves the shortest route when that costs almost nothing.

## The cost of a hot metre

```{python}
#| output: asis
bh = pd.DataFrame(s10["by_hour"]).set_index("label")
k = [f"{d[5:7]}{d[8:10]}_{cfg['study']['key_hour']:02d}" for d in cfg["study"]["dates"]]
us, ub = bh.loc[k, "u_sun"].mean(), bh.loc[k, "u_bldg"].mean()
print(f"""The coolest walk keeps θ but values each metre by its UTCI:

$$C_{{\\text{{heat}}}} = \\sum_{{\\text{{edges}}}} L\\,(1 - \\theta\\,r), \\qquad r = \\frac{{U_{{\\text{{sun}}}} - U}}{{U_{{\\text{{sun}}}} - U_{{\\text{{building}}}}}}$$

$U$ is the sidewalk's UTCI; $U_{{\\text{{sun}}}}$ and $U_{{\\text{{building}}}}$ are the city medians in sun and in building shade at that hour
(15:00: about {us:.1f} and {ub:.1f} °C). A typically sunny metre costs 1 and a typically building-shaded one 1 − θ, as in the shade
cost; everything in between follows its UTCI ($r$ kept between −1 and 1.5). Indoor passages have no UTCI, so the coolest walk stays
outdoors.""")
```

```{python}
d = s6["direction_check"]
print(f"\nThe direction does not matter: walking home to stop instead gives a mean sun reduction of {pct(d['sun_red_mean_home_to_stop'])} "

```

## Metrics

| Metric | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| **Sun** | |
| Sun share | metres in the sun on the shortest walk ÷ its length |
| Sun reduction | (sun on shortest − sun on shadiest) ÷ sun on shortest |
| Weighted exposure reduction | (C of shortest − C of shadiest) ÷ C of shortest |
| No cooler option | the shadiest walk avoids less than 2% of the sun |
| **Heat** | |
| UTCI of a walk | length-weighted mean UTCI along it, in °C |
| UTCI reduction | UTCI of the shortest − UTCI of the coolest (or shadiest) walk, in °C |
| Extreme heat stress | metres with UTCI ≥ 46 °C |
| **Both** | |
| Detour | (length of the walk − shortest length) ÷ shortest length |
| Indoor Contribution Index | (1 − L<sub>shadiest</sub> ÷ L<sub>shortest, outdoor</sub>) × indoor share of the shadiest path's shade (Wen et al. 2025) |

Weighted exposure falls about a tenth as much as sun: with θ near 0.2, each metre of sun avoided lowers C by only 0.15–0.2 m.

## Indoor scenarios (University City)

Mapped entrances are linked to the nearest sidewalk; passages through buildings count as indoor walking. Three cases: outdoor only, plus buildings open without a Penn ID, plus all mapped buildings. The shortest route is always the outdoor one.

## How we checked

The five stations with the largest sun reduction were checked on aerial photos; checks of the heat model are in the [technical notes](technical.qmd).
